docs.text: the ocean is pretty cool i guess reminds me of lake michigan
First time I saw the Pacific I was eight. I was unimpressed. I'd been living on the shores of Lake Erie. The only evident difference was a different stink.
The Lake is a deep and glorious aquamarine today.
I liked imagining a river so wide you can't see the other side. I've never seen one. (I was surprised when I saw Lake Michigan, though.)

I adore the ocean - it has a different feeling than the Great Lakes and I love shell hunting. But it's comical when people try to claim we don't have "real" beaches or "real" waves. Our waves are different - they're faster and harder to surf on, but they're most certainly real.
Stopped at a small park next to Lake Michigan on my way home. Having lived my entire life in Iowa, my brain struggles to comprehend the sight of water with no visible land on the other side.
Did you take this picture yourself? I have never seen the ocean. Lake Michigan is the closest I've come (size wise).
I will say that from the times I've been in Chicago, Lake Michigan really does LOOK like the Ocean. It's not though 😂

I remember when I first moved to Chicago I thought Lake Michigan was a big, flat, body of water that just sat there. Little did I know! The first time I saw large waves I realized that, no, it wasn’t the Atlantic Ocean of my childhood, it was still formidable. And it’s really cool!
I wouldn't know. I've never lived by an ocean. The worst Lake Michigan has ever done weather wise is crest over LSD, but it happens very rarely.
I've seen the Pacific, when I was in Seattle for a conference, but haven't been in those waters, no. I live near Lake Ontario, so even the Atlantic is hours away

As a Midwesterner, the concept of the ocean is terrifying. With the exception of the Great Lakes, when it comes to bodies of water, I like being able to see across to the other side. Puts my mind at ease.

Call of the sea is real. Thinking about looking out at Lake Michigan while we were in Chicago. Thinking about the time she almost killed my father and I while taking a boat down to Chicago. Thinking about the Mackinac Race that almost claimed my father's life. Thinking about boat names.
Yeah. I was a kid in Cleveland. We moved to Los Angeles when I was eight. I was not impressed with the Pacific Ocean. Didn't really look any bigger than Lake Erie, just stank different.
